metrics.doc: (standard[maker|taker] + standard[buyer|seller]) x discount + (tax[...] + tax[...]) + (special[...] + special[...]). The discount multiplier applies only when the account and the symbol have it enabled and the fee was paid in the discount asset; it never applies to tax or special commissions (Binance Commission FAQ). Example from the FAQ: taker sell, standard 0.0000002 + 0.0000004, tax 0.00000114 + 0.00000116, special 0.02 + 0.04, discount 0.25 gives 0.06000245.

D x (fill - mid) / mid x 10,000. The distance from the mid that the fill paid. A taker normally pays about half the quoted spread. A negative value means price improvement, or a maker fill that earned the spread. Example: buy at 100.02 with mid 100.01 gives 0.9999 bps.

Effective half-spread divided by the quoted half-spread, where the quoted half-spread is (quoted spread / 2) / mid x 10,000 and the quoted spread is max(ask proxy - bid proxy, one tick). 1.0 means the fill paid exactly the quoted half-spread; below 1.0 is price improvement. Not available when the quote is not two-sided.

D x (mid after h - mid at fill) / mid at fill x 10,000. How far the mid moved in the direction of the trade within h seconds. It coincided with the trade; the measurement does not show causation. Example: buy, mid 100.01, mid 15 s later 100.04 gives 2.9997 bps.

D x (fill - mid after h) / mid at fill x 10,000, for h = 1, 15, 60 and 300 seconds. The part of the effective half-spread that was still a cost after the market had h seconds to move. Example: buy at 100.02, mid 100.01, mid 15 s later 100.04 gives -1.9998 bps.

Execution + unfilled cost + fees, each divided by ordered quantity x arrival mid, x 10,000 (Perold 1988). Execution = sum D (fill - arrival mid) x qty, split into spread = sum D (fill - mid at fill) x qty and impact/timing = sum D (mid at fill - arrival mid) x qty. Unfilled cost = D (end mid - arrival mid) x unfilled qty: 0 for a fully filled order, unknown without an order record. Delay cost is not computed (no decision time). Example: buy 2.0 at arrival 100.00, fills 1.0 at 100.02 and 0.5 at 100.04, end mid 100.10, fees 0.15 gives execution 2.0, unfilled cost 2.5, fees 7.5, total 12.0 bps.

scoring.anchorRule: Anchors are the 10th, 50th, 90th and 99th percentiles of a public-market baseline; they score 100, 75, 40 and 0, linear in between.

components.fees: The fee paid (bps of notional) against the lowest rate the account had for that fill, from the account's own commission snapshot: 100 at or below that rate, falling linearly to 0 at twice it. A snapshot is the rate when it was fetched, so it is applied only to fills within 30 days of it; other fills read "not measured". On a zero-fee pair the reference is the exchange's published taker rate.
components.slippage: How far the mid moved against the order between the order's arrival and its fills, with the spread taken out (impact/timing, bps of the intended notional). Mapped through anchors from the signed mid drift of a random-side entry over the same duration, so 75 is the market median. For fast fills this is mostly market movement during the order, not a choice the trader made.
components.spread: The effective half-spread a taker event paid (bps): the fills of one order in one millisecond, at their volume-weighted price, against the mid just before that millisecond. Mapped through anchors from the same measure on public taker events (consecutive prints with the same millisecond and side, which is how one order that walks several price levels appears) of a similar total size. Half a tick or less scores 100. Each quote proxy may be up to 5 s old, for the fill and the baseline alike; on the M1 calibration days, including events with proxies older than 1 s coincided with a 12% (ETH) and 18% (BNB) higher 90th percentile for small events and left the medians almost unchanged. Version v2.0.0 scored each fill alone against single public prints.
components.timing: How much more the fill's UTC hour cost than the symbol's cheapest hours, in bps. An hour's cost is the median effective half-spread of public taker events that started in it (calibration days); the reference is the mean of the 3 cheapest hours. An excess of up to one price step scores 100. Above that step the excess is converted to points on the spread ladder of the fill's size class (the market-median event re-scored at its median plus the excess, divided by 75). Hours are not ranked, so hours that cost almost the same score the same; where nearly every event pays half a tick, every hour scores 100.
